resumen: Qué tiempo verbal pide cada marcador: yesterday, ago e in 2020 (pasado); now, at the moment, currently y these days (continuo); already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for y so far (perfecto); tomorrow, next week, soon e in two days (futuro). Y dónde van already, yet, still y just.

teoria.paraQue: Para que el marcador de tiempo te diga qué tiempo verbal usar antes de abrir la boca. Si dices yesterday, el verbo va en pasado; si dices already, va en perfecto; si dices tomorrow, va en futuro. El marcador es la señal de tráfico del verbo.
teoria.llave: La llave es el marcador: él elige el tiempo. Tiempo cerrado (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020) → pasado simple. Momento presente (now, at the moment, currently, these days) → presente continuo. Periodo abierto o resultado (already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, so far) → presente perfecto con have/has. Lo que viene (tomorrow, next week, soon, later, in two days) → futuro con will o going to. Aprende cada marcador con su tiempo pegado.

formulas.formula: yesterday / last week / two years ago / in 2020 / the other day + pasado simple
formulas.ejemplo: I {{sent}} the proposal yesterday. We {{moved}} to Bogotá in 2020.

formulas.formula: now / right now / at the moment / currently / these days + be + -ing
formulas.ejemplo: We[['re]] {{work((ing))}} on a pitch at the moment.

formulas.formula: have/has + already / just / never / ever + participio · … yet (al final)
have/has + participio + since + inicio / for + cantidad · so far / lately / recently
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ve]] {{worked}} here since 2020, for six years. So far we[['ve]] {{won}} three accounts.

formulas.formula: tomorrow / next week / soon / later / in two days / tonight + will / going to / be + -ing
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ll]] {{call}} you tomorrow. We[['re]] {{present((ing))}} next week.

formulas.formula: still antes del verbo y después de be · anymore al final, solo en negativas
by Friday (a más tardar) · until 6 (hasta) · during the meeting (durante) · on time (puntual) · in time (con margen)
formulas.ejemplo: I[['ll]] {{send}} it by Friday. I[['ll]] {{be}} here until 6.

reglas: Si el marcador cierra el tiempo (yesterday, last night, last week, two years ago, in 2020, the other day), el verbo va en pasado simple. Nunca have + yesterday.
Ago va después de la cantidad: two years ago, ten minutes ago. Y siempre con pasado simple.
Now, right now, at the moment, currently y these days piden presente continuo: lo que está pasando ahora o una tendencia temporal.
Already, just, ever y never van entre have y el participio: I've already sent it, Have you ever been…? Yet va al final, solo en negativas y preguntas: I haven't finished yet.
Since + punto de inicio (since 2020, since Monday); for + cantidad (for six years, for two hours). Los dos responden a How long…? y van con presente perfecto si el periodo sigue abierto.
So far, lately, recently y before (al final) piden presente perfecto porque el periodo sigue abierto o importa el resultado hoy.
Tomorrow, next week, soon, later, tonight e in two days (dentro de dos días) piden futuro: will para decisiones y promesas, going to o be + -ing para planes.
Still va antes del verbo y después de be: I still work there, I'm still waiting. Anymore va al final y solo en negativas: I don't work there anymore.
Nowadays pide presente simple (un hecho general de hoy). Eventually es «al final / con el tiempo», no «eventualmente». Finally es «por fin».
By Friday = a más tardar el viernes (plazo); until Friday = hasta el viernes (duración). On time = puntual; in time = a tiempo, con margen. During + nombre del evento, nunca + número.
Last, next, this, every, yesterday, tomorrow y tonight no llevan preposición: last week, next Monday, tonight (nunca in next week, in tonight).

usos.ejemplo: I {{went}} to the gym yesterday and I {{slept}} badly last night.

usos.uso: Decir qué estás haciendo estos días
usos.ejemplo: I[['m]] {{read((ing))}} a lot about AI these days.
I[['ve]] never {{been}} to the Amazon. [[Have]] you ever {{been}} there?
I[['m]] {{go((ing))}} to the gym tonight and we[['re]] {{travel((ing))}} to Santa Marta next week.

usos.uso: Dar el estado de un proyecto
usos.ejemplo: So far we[['ve]] {{finished}} the strategy, but the client [[has]]n't {{approved}} the budget yet.
I[['ll]] {{send}} you the files by Friday.
I[['ve]] {{worked}} at Brava since 2020, for six years.
We [[do]]n't {{work}} with print anymore. We[['ve]] recently {{hired}} two video editors.

errores.mal: I have sent the proposal yesterday.
errores.porque: Yesterday cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, nunca perfecto.

errores.mal: I am working at Brava since 2020.
errores.bien: I have worked at Brava since 2020.
errores.porque: Since pide presente perfecto, no continuo. En español «estoy trabajando desde» engaña.

errores.mal: We finished the video since two days.
errores.bien: We finished the video two days ago.
errores.porque: «Hace dos días» es ago, después de la cantidad.

errores.mal: I didn't finish yet the report.
errores.bien: I haven't finished the report yet.
errores.porque: Yet va al final y con presente perfecto.
Tomorrow pide futuro: will. El presente simple es para horarios fijos.
«Ya no» es anymore al final. Still va antes del verbo y significa «todavía sigo».

errores.mal: I'll be in the office by 6 pm, all afternoon.
errores.bien: I'll be in the office until 6 pm.
errores.porque: Until es hasta (duración); by es a más tardar (plazo).

contraste.nota: Yesterday cierra el tiempo (pasado). Just mira el resultado hoy (perfecto).
Pasado + for: ya terminó. Perfecto + for: sigo ahí.
Still = todavía sigue. Anymore = ya no (al final, negativa).
By = fecha límite. Until = hasta ese momento, todo el tiempo.

contraste.b: We {{arrived}} in time for the meeting.
contraste.nota: On time = puntual, a la hora. In time = a tiempo, con margen.

frases.en: I'll get back to you tomorrow.
We haven't received the feedback yet.
frases.es: Todavía no hemos recibido la retroalimentación.

frases.en: I've just sent you the files.
I need it by Friday at the latest.
frases.es: Lo necesito a más tardar el viernes.

frases.en: We're currently working on three campaigns.
frases.es: Actualmente estamos trabajando en tres campañas.

frases.en: I'm still waiting for the client's approval.
frases.es: Todavía estoy esperando la aprobación del cliente.

frases.en: Have you ever been to Cartagena?
Long time no see! How long has it been?

teoria.tip: Mira el marcador antes que el verbo. Si tiene fecha o «ago», es pasado. Si dice «ya, todavía, desde, alguna vez», es perfecto. Si dice «ahora», es continuo. Si mira al futuro, will. El marcador elige el tiempo; tú solo obedeces.

palabras.ejemplo: I sent the proposal yesterday.
palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple: el tiempo está cerrado. Nunca con have.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll call you tomorrow.
palabras.nota: Pide futuro: will, going to o presente continuo con plan.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm working on the budget now.
palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo: algo que pasa en este momento.

palabras.ejemplo: She joined Brava two years ago.
palabras.nota: Va después de la cantidad (two years ago) y pide pasado simple, nunca perfecto.

palabras.ejemplo: I've already sent the invoice.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: The client hasn't approved the budget yet.

hueco.frase: The client hasn't approved the budget ___. (todavía)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto en negativas y preguntas. Va al final de la frase.

palabras.ejemplo: We've just finished the presentation.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto: have + just + participio. En EE. UU. también se oye con pasado simple.

palabras.ejemplo: We launched the campaign last week.

hueco.frase: We launched the campaign ___. (la semana pasada)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple. Sin preposición: nunca «in last week». Igual last month, last year.

palabras.ejemplo: We're presenting to the client next week.

hueco.frase: We're presenting to the client ___. (la próxima semana)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro. Sin preposición: nunca «in next week». Igual next month, next year.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm still waiting for the client's answer.

hueco.frase: I'm ___ waiting for the client's answer. (todavía)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo o presente simple. Va antes del verbo y después de be.

palabras.ejemplo: Laura is in a meeting at the moment.

hueco.frase: Laura is in a meeting ___. (en este momento)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo (o be en presente). Equivale a right now.

palabras.ejemplo: I've worked at Brava since 2020.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto. Since + fecha o momento de inicio.

palabras.ejemplo: I've lived in Chapinero for six years.

hueco.frase: I've lived in Chapinero ___ six years. (durante / hace)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto cuando el periodo sigue abierto (for six years = y sigo). Con pasado simple si ya terminó.

palabras.ejemplo: Have you ever worked with a bank?

hueco.frase: Have you ___ worked with a bank? (alguna vez)

palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto en preguntas de experiencia. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: I've never been to the Amazon.
palabras.nota: Con have pide presente perfecto: experiencia que no has tenido. Va entre have y el participio.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll send you the files soon.
palabras.nota: Pide futuro con will. See you soon.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll finish the report later.
palabras.nota: Pide futuro, casi siempre will. Talk to you later.

palabras.ejemplo: I'm going to the gym tonight.

hueco.frase: I'm going to the gym ___. (esta noche)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: going to o presente continuo con plan.

palabras.ejemplo: I slept badly last night.
palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple. Nunca «yesterday night».

palabras.ejemplo: We moved to Bogotá in 2020.
palabras.nota: Un año cerrado pide pasado simple. Si quieres «desde 2020», es since + perfecto.

palabras.ejemplo: We're currently working with three clients.
palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo. Ojo: no significa «corrientemente».

palabras.ejemplo: Everyone is talking about AI these days.

hueco.frase: Everyone is talking about AI ___. (en estos días)

palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo: una tendencia temporal.

palabras.ejemplo: We've recently hired two designers.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto (va entre have y participio o al final). Con una fecha concreta, pasado simple.

palabras.ejemplo: I haven't slept well lately.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto, sobre todo en negativas y preguntas. Va al final.

palabras.ejemplo: So far we've received ten proposals.
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto: el periodo sigue abierto.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll send you the files by Friday.

hueco.frase: I'll send you the files ___ Friday. (a más tardar el)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: una fecha límite. No es until.

palabras.ejemplo: I'll be at the office until 7.
palabras.nota: Marca el fin de una duración; va con cualquier tiempo. Para plazos usa by.

palabras.ejemplo: Please don't check your phone during the meeting.

hueco.frase: Please don't check your phone ___ the meeting. (durante)

palabras.nota: During + el nombre del evento (the meeting, the trip). Con cantidades (two hours) es for. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.ejemplo: We had lunch and then we went back to the office.

hueco.frase: We had lunch and ___ we went back to the office. (luego)

palabras.nota: Ordena una historia en pasado simple. También «en esa época»: I was a student then.

palabras.ejemplo: The meeting ended at 5 and afterwards we had a beer.

hueco.frase: The meeting ended at 5 and ___ we had a beer. (después)

palabras.nota: Pasado simple en una narración (o futuro en un plan). En EE. UU. también afterward.

palabras.ejemplo: I don't drink coffee at night anymore.

hueco.frase: I don't drink coffee at night ___. (ya no)

palabras.nota: Solo en negativas, al final. Pide presente simple: un hábito que terminó.

palabras.ejemplo: Nowadays most people watch series on their phones.

hueco.frase: ___ most people watch series on their phones. (hoy en día)

palabras.nota: Pide presente simple: un hecho general de la época actual.

palabras.ejemplo: The designers are finishing the layout; meanwhile, I'm writing the copy.

hueco.frase: The designers are finishing the layout; ___, I'm writing the copy. (mientras tanto)

palabras.nota: Dos acciones a la vez: pide continuo (presente o pasado). Va al inicio de la frase.

palabras.ejemplo: We'll eventually move to a bigger office.

hueco.frase: We'll ___ move to a bigger office. (con el tiempo)

palabras.nota: Futuro (will) o pasado simple. Ojo: no es «eventualmente» (eso es occasionally).

palabras.ejemplo: We've finally signed the contract!
palabras.nota: Perfecto cuando algo por fin se logró; pasado simple al cerrar una historia.

palabras.ejemplo: The meeting started on time.

hueco.frase: The meeting started ___ time. (puntual: a la hora)

palabras.nota: A la hora exacta, ni antes ni después. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.es: a tiempo (antes de que sea tarde)
palabras.ejemplo: We finished the video just in time for the launch.

hueco.frase: We finished the video just ___ time for the launch. (a tiempo: con margen)

palabras.nota: Con margen, antes del límite. Suele ir con for. Cualquier tiempo.

palabras.es: en dos días, dentro de dos días
palabras.ejemplo: The client arrives in two days.

hueco.frase: The client arrives ___ two days. (dentro de)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro: in + cantidad = dentro de. Nunca «within two days ago».

palabras.ejemplo: I ran into Mike the other day.

hueco.frase: I ran into Mike ___. (el otro día)

palabras.nota: Pide pasado simple: un día reciente no concreto.

palabras.ejemplo: Sorry, I can't talk right now.
palabras.nota: Pide presente continuo o presente simple con modales (I can't talk right now).

palabras.ejemplo: I'm working from home this week.
palabras.nota: Pide continuo si es algo temporal; perfecto si cuentas lo hecho hasta hoy (I've had three meetings this week).

palabras.ejemplo: I've seen this movie before.
palabras.nota: Al final de la frase pide presente perfecto: experiencia previa.

palabras.ejemplo: How long have you worked here?
palabras.nota: Pide presente perfecto; la respuesta lleva for o since.

palabras.ejemplo: The client is coming the day after tomorrow.
palabras.nota: Pide futuro. Lo contrario es the day before yesterday (pasado simple).

palabras.ejemplo: From now on, we'll send the report on Fridays.

hueco.frase: ___, we'll send the report on Fridays. (de ahora en adelante)

palabras.nota: Pide futuro con will: una regla nueva desde hoy.

ejercicios.explica: Yesterday cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, nunca perfecto.

ejercicios.q: We ___ on a new campaign at the moment.
ejercicios.explica: At the moment pide presente continuo: algo que pasa ahora.
Con have + participio, «ya» es already, entre have y el participio.

ejercicios.q: Have you ___ worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: «Alguna vez» en preguntas de experiencia es ever, entre have y el participio.
Tomorrow pide futuro: will + verbo base.
Un año cerrado va con in y pasado simple. Since pediría perfecto.
«Hace dos años» es two years ago: la cantidad primero y ago al final.

ejercicios.q: The client hasn't approved the budget ___.
ejercicios.explica: En negativas, «todavía no» es yet, al final de la frase.
Yesterday pide pasado simple: worked.
Next week pide futuro: will present, are going to present o are presenting (plan).
Since + inicio pide presente perfecto: have lived (o have been living).

ejercicios.frase: I'm reading a lot about AI these days.
ejercicios.explica: These days marca una tendencia temporal: presente continuo.

ejercicios.frase: Have you ever worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: Ever + have + participio: experiencia hasta hoy, sin fecha.
Cada marcador tiene su tiempo pegado: apréndelos en pareja.

ejercicios.frase: I have sent the proposal yesterday.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: We launched the campaign last week.
ejercicios.explica: Last week pide pasado simple: la frase está bien.

respuestas: I have just finished the report.
ejercicios.explica: Just va entre have y el participio: 've just finished.

ejercicios.en: I have already sent the invoice.
ejercicios.explica: Already va entre have y el participio sent. Yet sería para negativa o pregunta.

ejercicios.q: Last night I ___ (watch) a movie with my wife.
ejercicios.explica: Last night cierra el tiempo: pasado simple.

ejercicios.q: Right now we ___ (wait) for the client's feedback.
ejercicios.explica: Right now pide presente continuo: are waiting.
So far = hasta ahora: el periodo sigue abierto, presente perfecto.
In two days = dentro de dos días: futuro (will, going to, continuo) o presente simple si es un horario fijo.
Lately pide presente perfecto: haven't seen.
«Ya no» en negativa es anymore, al final.

ejercicios.q: I ___ at Brava for six years, and I love it here.
ejercicios.explica: For six years con el periodo abierto (sigo ahí) pide presente perfecto.

ejercicios.q: We ___ the budget during yesterday's meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday's meeting cierra el tiempo: pasado simple aunque haya during.
Later pide futuro con will: una promesa o decisión del momento.

ejercicios.es: Todavía estoy esperando la respuesta del cliente.
ejercicios.en: I'm still waiting for the client's answer.
ejercicios.explica: Still va después de be y antes del verbo -ing. Yet iría al final de una negativa.

ejercicios.es: ¿Alguna vez has trabajado con un banco?
ejercicios.en: Have you ever worked with a bank?
ejercicios.explica: Ever va entre have y el participio. Did pediría un momento concreto.

ejercicios.es: Te llamo mañana después de la reunión.
ejercicios.en: I'll call you tomorrow after the meeting.
ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow pide will: I'll call. Called es la trampa del pasado.

ejercicios.es: Hace dos años nos mudamos a Bogotá.
ejercicios.en: We moved to Bogotá two years ago.
ejercicios.explica: Ago va después de la cantidad y pide pasado simple: moved, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: I am working at Brava since 2020.
correccion: I have worked at Brava since 2020.
I have been working at Brava since 2020.
I've been working at Brava since 2020.
ejercicios.explica: Since pide presente perfecto, no presente continuo.

ejercicios.frase: We have finished the video two days ago.
correccion: We finished the video two days ago.
ejercicios.explica: Two days ago cierra el tiempo: pasado simple, sin have.

ejercicios.frase: I don't work with that client anymore.
ejercicios.explica: Anymore al final y en negativa: «ya no». La frase está bien.

ejercicios.frase: I have already send the invoice.
correccion: I have already sent the invoice.
ejercicios.explica: Already pide have + participio: sent, no send.

respuestas: I will send the files tomorrow.
I am going to send the files tomorrow.
I'm going to send the files tomorrow.
I am sending the files tomorrow.
ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow cambia el tiempo a futuro: will send, going to send o am sending.

respuestas: We have just finished the report.
ejercicios.explica: «Acabamos de» es have + just + participio. En EE. UU. también se oye We just finished.

ejercicios.es: Todavía no he terminado la presentación.
respuestas: I haven't finished the presentation yet.
I have not finished the presentation yet.
I still haven't finished the presentation.
I still have not finished the presentation.
ejercicios.explica: «Todavía no» = haven't + participio + yet (o still haven't).

respuestas: We are currently working with three clients.
We're currently working with three clients.
Currently we are working with three clients.
Currently, we are working with three clients.
Currently we're working with three clients.
Currently, we're working with three clients.
We are working with three clients currently.
We currently work with three clients.
Currently we work with three clients.
Currently, we work with three clients.
ejercicios.explica: Currently pide presente continuo: are currently working.
Soon mira al futuro: see you soon o I'll see you soon.

respuestas: I didn't sleep well last night.
I did not sleep well last night.
Last night I didn't sleep well.
Last night I did not sleep well.
ejercicios.explica: Last night cierra el tiempo: pasado simple (slept / didn't sleep).

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta qué hiciste ayer, qué estás haciendo esta semana, qué has hecho hasta ahora en el proyecto y qué vas a hacer mañana.
ejercicios.objetivo: yesterday + pasado simple · this week / at the moment + presente continuo · so far / already + presente perfecto · tomorrow + will / going to
ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I had three meetings and I sent the budget to the client. This week I'm working on a pitch for a coffee brand. So far we've finished the strategy and we've already started the creative work. Tomorrow I'm going to present the first ideas to the team.
ejercicios.explica: Cada marcador manda su tiempo: yesterday → pasado; this week / at the moment → continuo; so far / already → perfecto; tomorrow → will / going to.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Yesterday I {1} (have) a long day at Brava. I {2} (get) to the office at 8 and we {3} (start) the status meeting on time. Right now I {4} (work) on the budget for a new client, and the designers {5} (finish) the layouts at the moment. We {6} (not / send) the proposal yet, but so far the client {7} (love) our ideas. Tomorrow I {8} (present) the final version.
ejercicios.explica: Yesterday y las horas cerradas → pasado; right now / at the moment → continuo; yet / so far → perfecto; tomorrow → futuro.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con la palabra o el verbo en el tiempo correcto.
ejercicios.texto: Camila is a copywriter from Cali. She moved to Bogotá three years {1} (hace), when she got her first job at an agency. She {2} (live) in Chapinero {3} (desde) 2023, in a small apartment with a big window, and she {4} (work) at a digital agency {5} (durante: cantidad) two years now. On weekends she {6} (already / visit) Medellín and Cartagena with friends from the office, but she {7} (never / be) to the Amazon, which is her dream trip. {8} (hasta ahora), she loves the city: the food, the people and even the rain.
ejercicios.explica: Ago cierra el tiempo (pasado); since / for / already / never / so far piden presente perfecto.

ejercicios.titulo: El plan de la próxima semana
ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la opción correcta en cada desplegable.
ejercicios.texto: Next week is going to be busy. On Monday we {1} the new campaign to the client. {2} we have the budget meeting with the finance team. The designers {3} the final layouts by Wednesday. I {4} from home on Thursday because my daughter has a school event. {5}, on Friday, we're having a team lunch to celebrate the launch. I {6} back to you with the final dates soon.
ejercicios.explica: Next week y los días que vienen piden futuro (be + -ing, will, going to); afterwards y finally ordenan el plan.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Last Saturday I {1} (wake) up late, around 10. I {2} (go) to the gym and then I {3} (have) lunch with my parents in Chía. Afterwards we {4} (walk) around the town for an hour. These days I {5} (try) to spend more time with my family, because I {6} (not / see) them much lately. Tonight I {7} (stay) home and watch a series.
ejercicios.explica: Last Saturday, then y afterwards → pasado simple; these days → continuo; lately → perfecto; tonight → futuro.

ejercicios.instruccion: Elige la opción correcta en cada desplegable.
ejercicios.texto: Hi Sarah, I hope you're well. I {1} the revised proposal on Monday afternoon, with the new budget and the updated timeline, but I {2} your feedback yet. On our side, we {3} finished the video {4}, and the team is {5} working on the social media posts and the landing page. Could you confirm the budget {6} Friday? We need the final approval {7} time for the launch on the 25th, because the media plan starts that same week. Thanks a lot, and talk soon! Andrés
ejercicios.explica: On Monday (fecha) → pasado; yet y already → perfecto; still → continuo; by para el plazo e in time para llegar con margen.

ejercicios.instruccion: Completa con el tiempo que pide cada marcador.
ejercicios.texto: Nowadays most of our clients {1} (want) short videos for social media. Five years ago, they {2} (ask) for TV commercials. At the moment we {3} (produce) around twenty videos a month, and so far this year we {4} (win) three new accounts. We {5} (not / work) with print anymore. Next month we {6} (hire) two more editors, and eventually we {7} (open) a small studio.
ejercicios.explica: Nowadays → presente simple; five years ago → pasado; at the moment → continuo; so far this year → perfecto; anymore → presente negativo; next month / eventually → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Andrés is an account director at Brava. Last week he won a new client, a coffee brand from Huila, and yesterday he had the first meeting with their marketing team. At the moment his team is working on the strategy, and the designers are preparing three visual routes. So far the client has approved the budget and the timeline, but they haven't chosen a route yet. Andrés has already written the brief for the video, and tomorrow he's presenting the first ideas to the client's CEO. He needs the final approval by Friday, because the campaign launches in two weeks. He's a bit nervous, but so far, so good.

preguntas.q: When did Andrés win the coffee client?
What hasn't the client done yet?
When does Andrés need the final approval?
¿Por qué el texto dice «has approved» pero «had the first meeting»?
opciones: So far deja el periodo abierto (perfecto); yesterday lo cierra (pasado)
Approve siempre va en perfecto y have siempre en pasado
Son intercambiables; es cuestión de estilo

ejercicios.explica: Yesterday y last week → pasado; at the moment → continuo; so far / already / yet → perfecto; tomorrow / by Friday → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Mike has gone to the same gym since January, so he has been a member for almost a year. Two years ago he hardly did any exercise, and he didn't sleep well. Last month he finally ran his first 10K in Bogotá, and he has already signed up for another race in Medellín. He has never lifted weights before, but these days he is trying a strength program with a trainer. He hasn't missed a class lately, and he feels much better. From now on, he says, he will train four times a week and eat less fast food. His wife, Laura, is not so sure: she has heard that promise before.

preguntas.q: How long has Mike been a member of the gym?
What did Mike do last month?
opciones: He signed up for the gym

preguntas.q: What is Mike doing these days?
¿Por qué «he has gone … since January» pero «two years ago he hardly did any exercise»?
opciones: Since abre el periodo hasta hoy (perfecto); ago lo cierra en el pasado (pasado simple)
Go siempre va en perfecto y do en pasado
Porque since es formal y ago es informal

ejercicios.explica: Since / for / never / lately → perfecto; two years ago / last month → pasado; these days → continuo; from now on → futuro.

ejercicios.texto: Hi Camila, here is a quick update on the launch. We've already finished the TV spot and we've just sent the final cut to your team. The social media posts are still in production; the designers are working on the last three pieces right now. Tomorrow we're recording the radio spot, and next week we'll present the media plan to your board. We need your comments on the posts by Thursday, so we can deliver everything in time for the launch on the 25th. So far we are on schedule and on budget. I'll send you the final report soon. From now on, we'll have a short status call every Monday at 9. Thanks, Mike.

preguntas.q: What has the agency just sent?
opciones: The final cut of the TV spot

preguntas.q: When are they recording the radio spot?
Why does Mike need the comments by Thursday?
opciones: To deliver everything in time for the launch
Because the launch is on Thursday
Because the designers finish on Thursday

preguntas.q: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre «by Thursday» y «in time for the launch»?
opciones: By es el plazo máximo; in time es llegar con margen antes del evento
By es informal e in time es formal

ejercicios.explica: Tomorrow, next week, by Thursday y soon → futuro; already / just / so far → perfecto; still → continuo.

ejercicios.texto: Last weekend Laura and Andrés went to Santa Marta. They flew on Friday night and then they took a bus to Taganga. On Saturday they went snorkeling; afterwards they ate fish on the beach and slept until noon on Sunday. Laura had never been to the Caribbean before, and she loved it. Now they are planning a longer trip: at the moment they're looking at hotels in Palomino, but they haven't booked anything yet. Andrés still has two weeks of vacation this year, so they're going back next month, probably with Laura's parents. They don't travel by bus anymore, though: next time they'll rent a car.

preguntas.q: How did they get to Taganga?
opciones: They flew to Santa Marta and then took a bus
They took a bus from Bogotá

preguntas.q: Had Laura been to the Caribbean before this trip?
What are they doing at the moment?
¿Por qué «they haven't booked anything yet» va en perfecto?
opciones: Yet deja el resultado abierto hasta hoy

ejercicios.explica: Last weekend / then / afterwards → pasado; now / at the moment → continuo; never / yet → perfecto; next month → futuro.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe sobre tu semana: qué hiciste ayer (yesterday), qué estás haciendo esta semana o ahora mismo (this week, right now) y qué harás mañana o la próxima semana.

requisitos.texto: Usa yesterday con un verbo en pasado
Usa this week, right now, at the moment o these days
Usa tomorrow, next week, soon o later
Usa will, 'll o going to para el futuro

ejercicios.ejemplo: Yesterday I had two client meetings and I sent the budget for the new campaign. This week I'm working on a pitch for a bank, so right now I'm reading a lot about financial apps. Tomorrow I'll present the first ideas to my team, and next week we're going to show them to the client.
ejercicios.explica: Cada marcador elige su tiempo: yesterday + pasado, this week / right now + continuo, tomorrow + will / going to.

ejercicios.consigna: Cuenta tu experiencia en tu trabajo actual: cuánto tiempo llevas (for / since), qué has logrado hasta ahora (already, so far, just) y qué no has hecho todavía (yet).

requisitos.texto: Usa for o since con presente perfecto
Usa already, just, so far, ever o never
Usa yet al final de una negativa

ejercicios.ejemplo: I have worked at Brava since 2020, so I've been here for six years. So far I've led campaigns for a bank, a coffee brand and two retail clients. I've already built a team of eight people and we have just won a new account. I haven't worked with an international client yet, but I have never stopped learning, and I'd love to try.
ejercicios.explica: Since / for abren el periodo; already / just / so far cuentan lo logrado; yet al final de la negativa cierra lo pendiente.

ejercicios.consigna: Escribe un correo corto a un cliente con los próximos pasos del proyecto: qué harán la próxima semana, qué enviarán y para cuándo (by…), y qué pasará después (afterwards, then, eventually).

requisitos.texto: Usa next week, tomorrow, in two days o soon
Usa by + día o fecha para el plazo
Usa afterwards, then, eventually o finally

ejercicios.ejemplo: Hi Sarah, here are the next steps. Next week we're going to record the video and we'll send you the first cut by Friday. Then your team can review it, and we will make the changes in two days. Afterwards, we'll prepare the social media posts and the media plan. Eventually, the full campaign will be ready by the end of the month. Talk to you soon, Andrés.
ejercicios.explica: Next week / in two days / soon piden futuro; by marca el plazo; afterwards, then y eventually ordenan los pasos.
